note: v2 — segment 4 retravaillé : chaque épisode a un plan preuve unique et cohérent avec son thème. Champ de bataille conservé UNIQUEMENT quand le texte parle de destruction de masse (ep02, 03, 13). Production un par un, pas en batch.

segments.voice: You just lost. And right now — you want it back.
segments.plan: orage seul → éclair révèle perso de dos

segments.voice: That feeling has a name… revenge. And the market — loves it.
A manager never trades to get even. He trades… to get paid.
Every blown account I've ever seen… died on a revenge trade. Every — single — one.
segments.plan: champ de bataille (destruction de masse = cohérent)

segments.voice: Next time you want revenge… walk away. That's how you strike back.
Your account is small. But your ego… is huge. That's why you're broke.
Size isn't about money. It's about humility. I run real capital — I size like I could be wrong.
Ten percent a day… isn't a goal. It's a countdown.
Nine out of ten blow up… chasing size they can't hold.
Trade small. Think big. Or the market teaches you… the hard way.
There's a villain who never raises his voice. He doesn't need to — he bleeds you in silence.
segments.plan: orage → éclair révèle couloir feutré, porte qui se ferme

segments.voice: They call him the Aristocrat. Euro-Dollar. He lures you into his range… and waits.
He doesn't spike. He doesn't crash. He just… drains. Slowly. Until you overtrade yourself to death.
segments.plan: corps assis, profil, cigare dans un cendrier

segments.voice: Most traders don't even realize he's killing them. They think they're trading — they're just feeding him.
segments.plan: couloir d'hôtel vide, lumières qui s'éteignent une par une vers le fond — l'Aristocrate t'endort

segments.voice: Learn his pattern — or keep paying his rent.
You don't lose randomly. You lose… the exact same way. Every time.
segments.plan: orage → éclair révèle perso de dos devant des écrans

segments.voice: Same setup. Same mistake. Same excuse. You've told yourself it was different — it wasn't.
The market doesn't beat you with new tricks. It beats you — with your own.
Open your journal. Last ten losses. Same entry. Same flaw. You already know.
segments.plan: gros plan sur un carnet ouvert sous une lampe, pages qui se tournent — le pattern écrit noir sur blanc

segments.voice: Stop blaming the market for a wound you keep reopening. Read your own pattern.
Last night… another one packed his desk.
segments.plan: orage → éclair révèle bureau vide, chaise qui tourne

segments.voice: Ten years in this game — gone… in one trade. One size he couldn't hold.
The desk stays empty. The market — doesn't notice.
segments.plan: corps de dos, regarde la baie vitrée

segments.voice: I've watched it happen to better traders than you. Better than me. Nobody's safe — unless they choose to be.
segments.plan: rangée de bureaux vides, open space désert, une seule lampe encore allumée au fond

segments.voice: If your chair is still warm… respect it. Or be the next empty desk.
You took twelve trades today. You needed — one.
segments.plan: orage → éclair révèle perso assis, tête baissée

segments.voice: More trades doesn't mean more money. It means more exposure… to your own mistakes.
A sniper fires once. A gambler — fires until he's empty.
The best month I ever had… I traded nine times. Nine — in thirty days.
segments.plan: écran unique dans le noir, curseur immobile — le calme d'un mois à 9 trades

segments.voice: Put the gun down. Wait for the shot that matters. Quality kills quantity.
Some villains take their time. This one — doesn't.
segments.plan: orage → éclair révèle ruelle sous la pluie, néon de pub

segments.voice: The Cable. Pound-Dollar. Fast, violent, no warning. He hits — and he's gone before you blink.
The Aristocrat bleeds you slowly. The Cable — breaks you on the spot.
segments.plan: corps de dos, pluie sur la vitre

segments.voice: Fifty-pip spike on a Tuesday. No news. No reason. That's his signature — chaos disguised as noise.
segments.plan: ruelle de Londres sous la pluie, néon de pub qui grésille et s'éteint d'un coup — la violence du Cable

segments.voice: You don't fight the Cable. You survive him.
You moved your stop. You told yourself — just a little more room. That's the last thought before the blow.
segments.plan: orage → éclair révèle perso, main sur le front

segments.voice: A stop loss isn't a suggestion. It's the only promise you make to yourself — that you'll walk away alive.
The stop was right where you put it. You moved it — because you couldn't accept being wrong.
Every account that ever blew up… had a stop loss. It just — wasn't there anymore when it mattered.
segments.plan: bureau abandonné, écran rouge figé, chaise repoussée — quelqu'un est parti en urgence

segments.voice: Set it. Leave it. Live to trade tomorrow. Discipline doesn't feel good — it feels like surviving.
You think doing nothing means you're losing. That's why — you keep losing.
segments.plan: orage → éclair révèle perso immobile, bras croisés

segments.voice: Cash is a position. Sitting out — is a trade. The hardest one you'll ever make.
The market pays patience — and taxes excitement.
My best weeks… I didn't trade. I watched. I waited. And when they moved — I was ready. They weren't.
segments.plan: ville vue d'en haut la nuit, immobile, lumières lentes — le calme avant le mouvement

segments.voice: Stop confusing action with progress. Cash is a position too.
I write every trade. Every win. Every loss. Every excuse I almost believed.
segments.plan: orage → éclair révèle bureau, carnet ouvert

segments.voice: The journal doesn't lie. You do. It remembers — what you're trying to forget.
You don't journal to track your P&L. You journal — to track your mind.
segments.plan: corps penché sur le bureau, profil

segments.voice: Six months of journal entries showed me I was making the same mistake… every single Thursday.
segments.plan: insert statique : carnet ouvert sous une lampe, stylo posé à côté — les preuves écrites

segments.voice: Write it down. Face what's in there. The truth is expensive — ignorance costs more.
You said it was the market. It wasn't. You said it was the broker. It wasn't. You're lying — to yourself.
segments.plan: orage → éclair révèle perso face miroir

segments.voice: The story you tell yourself after a loss… is more dangerous than the loss itself.
Blame is a painkiller. It feels good — and it stops you from healing.
I blamed the market for two years. The day I stopped — everything changed. Not the market. Me.
segments.plan: miroir dans un bureau sombre, reflet flou d'une silhouette — le mensonge qu'on se raconte

segments.voice: Stop telling yourself stories. Start reading the truth.
You're down twenty percent. And the voice in your head says — trade bigger. Win it back.
segments.plan: orage → éclair révèle perso assis dans le noir

segments.voice: A drawdown isn't a problem. What you DO in a drawdown — that's the problem.
Cut your size. Slow down. Survive the storm — then rebuild. Never the other way around.
segments.plan: corps profil, pluie sur la vitre

segments.voice: The ones who doubled down in a drawdown… never came back. The ones who halved their size — always did.
segments.plan: champ de bataille (ceux qui ne sont jamais revenus = destruction de masse cohérente)

segments.voice: Drawdowns don't kill traders. Pride does. Shrink before you grow.
He doesn't follow rules. He doesn't follow logic. He just — explodes.
segments.plan: orage → éclair révèle buildings, lumières qui clignotent

segments.voice: US Thirty. The Madman. Three hundred points on a single sentence from the Fed. No warning. No mercy.
You can't read him. You can't predict him. You can only — respect the distance.
segments.plan: corps de dos, écrans qui strobent

segments.voice: He's destroyed more accounts in a minute… than the others do in a month. And he'll do it again — tomorrow.
segments.plan: skyline de nuit, toutes les lumières d'un building qui s'éteignent d'un coup — le blackout du Madman

segments.voice: Some villains you fight. This one — you avoid.
You planned your entry. Your target. Your profit. But not — your exit if you're wrong.
segments.plan: orage → éclair révèle perso debout, bras croisés

segments.voice: Amateurs plan the win. Professionals — plan the loss.
Before you ask how much you can make… ask how much you can lose. That number — runs the trade.
segments.plan: corps profil, main sur le menton

segments.voice: I define my risk before I see my reward. If the risk doesn't fit — the trade doesn't exist.
segments.plan: échiquier vu de haut, pièces positionnées, une seule case vide au centre — la position calculée

segments.voice: Risk first. Everything else second. That's the order that keeps you alive.
You had a plan this morning. By noon — you'd broken every rule in it.
segments.plan: orage → éclair révèle perso devant un écran, tête dans les mains

segments.voice: A plan you don't follow — is just decoration. It sits there making you feel prepared… while you improvise.
The plan isn't the hard part. Following it when you're losing — that's the hard part.
segments.plan: corps de dos, baie vitrée nocturne

segments.voice: Every trader has a plan. Five percent follow it. Guess which five percent are still here.
segments.plan: feuilles de papier éparpillées sur un bureau, vent qui entre par la fenêtre — le plan abandonné

segments.voice: Write it. Follow it. No exceptions.
You opened three trades. You thought — you were diversified. You were tripling your risk.
segments.plan: orage → éclair révèle trois écrans allumés dans le noir

segments.voice: Three dollar pairs moving together isn't three trades. It's one trade — wearing three masks.
Correlation is the risk you don't see — until every position moves against you at the same time.
One DXY move… and all three trades died together. Same reason. Same second. Same grave.
segments.plan: trois lampes alignées sur un bureau qui s'éteignent l'une après l'autre — simultanéité de la perte

segments.voice: Know what you're actually risking. See the invisible thread — before it hangs you.
The dirtiest villain doesn't trade fair. He doesn't even pretend.
segments.plan: orage → éclair révèle silhouette dans la fumée industrielle

segments.voice: Oil. The Baron. He moves on geopolitics, on supply lies, on rumors — and when you think he's done… he spikes again.
The Baron doesn't need your analysis. He runs on forces — you can't even see from your chart.
Forty-six thousand… gone in sixteen seconds. Real money. Real loss. That's the Baron's signature.
segments.plan: flamme industrielle dans la nuit, fumée noire qui monte — la violence brute du pétrole

segments.voice: Oil doesn't care about your stop. It doesn't care about your plan. Respect the Baron — or don't trade him.
The candle moved without you. And now — you're chasing it.
segments.plan: orage → éclair révèle perso debout, penché vers l'écran

segments.voice: Fear of missing out — isn't about the trade you missed. It's about the pain of watching someone else win.
The best traders I know… miss trades every day. They sleep fine.
segments.plan: corps profil, café à la main

segments.voice: Every late entry I've ever taken out of FOMO — every single one — was worse than the trade I missed.
segments.plan: porte d'ascenseur qui se ferme lentement, personne dedans — le train est parti, et c'est ok

segments.voice: Miss the trade. Keep the capital. There's always another setup.
You didn't hold your trade because you had conviction. You held it — because you had ego.
segments.plan: orage → éclair révèle perso immobile dans le noir

segments.voice: Conviction says — I've done the work, and the evidence supports this position. Ego says — I can't be wrong.
One has a stop loss. The other — doesn't.
segments.plan: corps profil, regard vers le bas

segments.voice: I've had conviction and been wrong. The difference — I walked away with my capital. Ego would have buried it.
segments.plan: bureau calme après la tempête, chaise repoussée, écran éteint — le trade est fini, le capital est intact

segments.voice: Ask yourself — right now. Is it conviction… or ego. Learn the difference before it costs you.
You thought you were trading against the market. You're not. You're trading — against the house.
segments.plan: orage → éclair révèle néons de casino dans le noir

segments.voice: The brokers. They built the table. They wrote the rules. And when you start winning… they change them.
Slippage. Spread widening. Requotes. It's not a bug — it's the business model.
Thirty lots filled instantly on entry. On exit — sixteen seconds of silence. That's not execution. That's selection.
segments.plan: table de poker vide, cartes retournées face cachée, une seule lampe au-dessus — le jeu est truqué

segments.voice: Know who's dealing the cards. The house always does.
You want to double your account this month. You'll have — no account next month.
segments.plan: orage → éclair révèle perso assis, doigts croisés

segments.voice: Compounding doesn't need heroics. It needs — consistency. Small gains. Protected capital. Time.
Two percent a week — doesn't sound exciting. Until you do the math over a year.
The traders who survive ten years… don't have the best win rate. They have the best — staying rate.
segments.plan: ville à l'aube, lumière qui monte lentement sur les buildings — la construction silencieuse

segments.voice: Be boring. Be consistent. Be here next year. Compounding rewards the ones who don't quit.
My best trade this week — was silence.
segments.plan: orage → éclair révèle bureau vide, écrans éteints

segments.voice: No setup met my criteria. No edge appeared. So I did — nothing. And I kept everything.
The market screams every day — buy me, sell me, do something. The professionals — don't listen.
segments.plan: corps dos, baie vitrée, ville silencieuse

segments.voice: Three days. Zero trades. Zero drawdown. When the setup came on Thursday — I had full capital. Full clarity.
segments.plan: bureau immaculé, pas un papier, écrans éteints, lumière naturelle — le vide comme arme

segments.voice: Doing nothing — is the hardest skill in trading. Master it.
You're risking five percent per trade — and wondering why your account is bleeding.
segments.plan: orage → éclair révèle perso de dos, horizon rouge

segments.voice: One percent risk. That's it. That's the entire secret — that nobody wants to hear.
One percent means — you can be wrong ten times in a row… and still be in the game.
I manage real capital. I risk — less than one percent. If it's good enough for real money… it's good enough for yours.
segments.plan: coffre-fort massif, porte épaisse entrouverte, lumière qui filtre — le capital protégé

segments.voice: Shrink your risk. Grow your account. The math doesn't lie.
Your trade is underwater. And you just — added more.
segments.plan: orage → éclair révèle perso penché, mains sur la table

segments.voice: Averaging down on a losing trade isn't strategy. It's negotiating — with a bullet.
If the trade was right at one lot — why does it need two? Because the market proved you wrong. And you doubled down — on wrong.
Adding to a winner is skill. Adding to a loser — is a funeral invitation.
segments.plan: parking souterrain, néons crus, une seule voiture qui s'éloigne — le dernier qui part

segments.voice: If it's going against you — cut it. Don't feed it.
Every blown account — has a story. And every story — starts the same way.
segments.plan: orage → éclair révèle parking vide la nuit

segments.voice: It starts with confidence. Then conviction. Then — stubbornness. Then the screen goes red and doesn't come back.
The graveyard of traders is full — of people who were right about the direction… and wrong about the size.
segments.plan: corps de dos, marche dans un couloir vide

segments.voice: They knew the entry. They knew the target. They just — couldn't survive the trip.
segments.plan: open space vide la nuit, rangée de bureaux déserts, écrans éteints un par un — le cimetière des traders

segments.voice: Don't become another story that starts the same way.
You hit your daily target. And then — you kept trading.
segments.plan: orage → éclair révèle perso debout, manteau, prêt à partir

segments.voice: You won. And you gave it back. Not because the market took it — because you couldn't stop.
Winners — quit. They hit the number. They close the screen. They leave.
segments.plan: corps de dos, marche vers la sortie

segments.voice: My best days end at ten AM. Screen off. Walk away. The gains are real — only if you keep them.
segments.plan: porte de bureau qui se ferme lentement, couloir vide derrière — celui qui part au bon moment

segments.voice: Hit your target. Walk away. Learn the discipline of enough.
Twenty-seven rules. You've heard them all. And you already know — which ones you break.
segments.plan: orage → éclair révèle perso face caméra, immobile

segments.voice: Knowing the rules was never the hard part. Living them — when you're losing, when you're scared, when you're angry — that's the war.
The market doesn't care how much you know. It only cares — how much you obey.
segments.plan: corps profil, silhouette contre la baie vitrée

segments.voice: I break my own rules too. The difference — I write it down. I face it. And I fix it. Every single time.
segments.plan: carnet ouvert sur un bureau, stylo posé, lumière d'aube qui entre — le rituel du gérant

segments.voice: This isn't content. This is a mirror. Look at it — or look away. The rules don't stop.
